 Michael Hogan, James Edward Olmos in Battlestar Galactica Image via Syfy

 By  
 Rob London 
 Published Nov 2, 2026, 5:21 PM EST 
 A cinematic obsessive with the filmic palate of a starving raccoon, Rob London will watch pretty much anything once. With a mind like a steel trap, he's an endless fount of movie and TV trivia, borne from a misspent youth of watching monster movies on TV, perusing the sun-faded goods at the local video rental shop, and staining his fingers with ink from the Video Movie Guide. Areas of interest include science fiction, film noir, horror flicks , '70s disaster pictures, Bond movies, '90s action , giant robots , dinosaurs, super heroes , and the exuberantly schlocky output of Cannon Films. He also enjoys both Star Trek and Star Wars  when they're good, and maybe even more when they're bad. As a Canadian, he also has a vested interest in Canadian movies and TV shows, especially the cheesier ones dubbed "Canuxploitation."
An expert on Marvel Comics, he has also written for the Official Handbook of the Marvel Universe , and is a member of the Marvel Research Team. He can frequently be found pontificating on comic-book continuity or bemoaning the misfortunes of the Toronto Maple Leafs on his Twitter account.

 One of the cheesiest science fiction franchises of the 1970s became one of the best sci-fi offerings of the early 21st century when Battlestar Galactica made its grand return in 2003. That series ended in 2009, and much discussion about a revival or reboot has surfaced ever since. Now, while a new TV series or movie may be as difficult to find as the thirteenth colony, there's something coming to tide fans over.

 Battlestar Galactica was created by Glen A. Larson in 1978; the original series centered around the last warship of the Twelve Colonies, the Battlestar Galactica, which led a colony of human survivors as they sought out the long-lost thirteenth colony: Earth. Opposing them were the destroyers of humanity, the chrome-plated robot Cylons. The ship was popular, but extremely expensive, so it was fondly remembered but short-lived. It was revived by Star Trek: Deep Space Nine veteran Ronald D. Moore for the Sci-Fi Channel in 2003. The new series reimagined the series as a post-9/11 meditation on paranoia, terrorism, and freedom; the Cylon menace was even more insidious in this series, because they could disguise themselves as human beings. That series ended in 2009, and was followed by a prequel series, Caprica , about the origin of the Cylons; it was cancelled after a single season.
 Now, something from the heights of Aughts-era Battlestar mania is back. Battlestar Galactica: The Board Game , which was originally released in 2008 and based on the revival series, is returning with a new edition from Ghost Galaxy Games . The game was originally designed by Corey Konieczka and released by Fantasy Flight Games; it was a great success, and eventually garnered three expansions. Ghost Galaxy is working on a new, updated edition of the game, and intends to launch a Kickstarter crowdfunding campaign in 2027.

 ▦︎ 
 The Matrix 
 The Resistance, Zion 
 You take the red pill, you stay in Wonderland, and I show you how deep the rabbit hole goes. 
 You would survive The Matrix because you were never fully sold on the version of reality you were handed. You notice the seams. You ask the second question. In a world built to keep people comfortable and incurious, that instinct is the whole fight, and it is why Morpheus would have found you long before you found him.

 Mad Max 
 The Wasteland 
 Oh, what a day. What a lovely day. 
 You would survive the Wasteland because you do not waste energy mourning the world that ended. You move, you improvise, and you are very good with whatever is bolted to the thing in front of you. Furiosa would let you drive. That is not a compliment anybody earns easily.

 Mad Max: Fury Road won six Academy Awards in 2016, more than any other film that year.
 George Miller storyboarded the entire film as roughly 3,500 panels before there was a
 script.
 The chase was shot almost entirely practical in the Namib Desert, with real vehicles and
 real stunt performers.
 Anya Taylor-Joy and Chris Hemsworth carried the prequel, Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga, in 2024.
 Keeps moving

 ◑︎ 
 Blade Runner 
 Los Angeles, 2049 
 All those moments will be lost in time, like tears in rain. 
 You would survive 2049 because you know how to be small in a very loud city. You keep your head down, you do the job, and you hold onto one private thing that belongs only to you. That quiet stubbornness is exactly what both Deckard and K run on, and it is what keeps either of them going when the case stops making sense.

 Blade Runner 2049 won Roger Deakins his first Oscar for cinematography, on his fourteenth
 nomination.
 The film also took Best Visual Effects, 35 years after Ridley Scott's 1982 original.
 Villeneuve shot it on large-format film and kept the fog and rain practical on set wherever
 he could.
 Three short films by Luke Scott and Shinichiro Watanabe bridge the 30-year gap between the
 two movies.

 ▲︎ 
 Dune 
 Arrakis 
 Fear is the mind-killer. Fear is the little-death that brings total obliteration. 
 You would survive Arrakis because you think in decades while everyone around you thinks in weeks. You read the room, you learn the customs, you wait. The desert does not reward speed. It rewards people who understand that patience is a weapon, which is the one lesson the Fremen never had to be taught.

 Hans Zimmer turned down Christopher Nolan's Tenet so he could score Dune instead.
 Dune: Part Two arrived in 2024 and brought in Austin Butler, Florence Pugh and Christopher
 Walken.
 David Lynch's 1984 version and Alejandro Jodorowsky's unmade one are both their

 ✦︎ 
 Star Wars 
 A Galaxy Far, Far Away 
 Rebellions are built on hope. 
 You would survive the galaxy because you never try to survive it alone. You collect people. You end up in the middle of other folks' problems and you stay anyway. Every version of this story, from the Falcon's crew to the Ghost's, runs on somebody exactly like that holding the group together.

 What's Next for 'Battlestar Galactica?
 Since Caprica ended in 2010, the Battlestar Galactica franchise has largely lain fallow. Mr. Robot creator Sam Esmail was working on a revival series at Peacock that would reportedly have taken place in the same continuity as the 2003 series; despite being in development for years, the series was shut down at the streamer in 2024 . It was to be shopped around to other broadcasters and streamers, but two years later, there have been no updates, meaning the project is likely as dead as Cally Henderson.
 A new edition of Battlestar Galactica: The Board Game is in the works. Stay tuned to Collider for future updates.'
